newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian Islamist chief held in Blida jail - report.
newsitem.headline: Algerian Islamist chief held in Blida jail - report.

text.p: The vice-president of Algeria's banned Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), Ali Benhadj, is being held in secrecy in a military jail in Blida south of Algiers, the French newspaper Le Monde said on Tuesday.

Benhadj has been held since 1991, and the human rights organisation Amnesty International has expressed concern that his family has had no news of him since he was transferred to a secret location in early 1995.
Exiled FIS leaders have said he is seriously ill.
Le Monde quoted unspecified reliable sources for its report and said that it had not been able to confirm it with Algerian authorities.
The paper said neither Benhadj's relatives nor his lawyers had been told of his whereabouts by the authorities.

A journalist for Algeria's APS news agency who revealed on an internal printer in February 1995 that Benhadj was being held in the southern desert region of Tamanrasset was sentenced to three years in jail by a military tribunal.

Benhadj was arrested in June 1991 after a general strike during which he had urged people to "stock any weapons" they came across. The Blida military tribunal sentenced him in July 1992 to 12 years in jail for armed plotting against the state.
Like FIS leader Abassi Madani, he was taken from jail to house arrest in 1994 as the government tried to negotiate. The two men were sent back to prison a few months later after the talks failed.
About 60,000 people have been killed in civil violence in Algeria since the cancellation in 1992 of a general election in which radical Islamists of the FIS had taken a commanding lead.
